description: Natural Hazards Research Summit 2024: Engineering Design of Emergent Vegetation to Mitigate Wave Overtopping is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Daniel Cox, Oregon State University (oregonstate.edu). This poster describes three studies that support the implementation of Nature-based Solutions (NbS), specifically emergent vegetation, for flood risk reduction. NbS are landscape features used for flood risk management. They are increasingly popular due to the additional benefits they confer beyond flood protection, including increased habitat and carbon storage. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-44b4-hf65. Keywords: Large Wave Flume and Directional Basin, mangroves, overtopping, performance-based design, hybrid structures, green/gray structures. Published 2024-06-28. Facility named: Large Wave Flume and Directional Wave Basin - Oregon State University. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0 (labelled "Creative Commons Attribution" on the DesignSafe project). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
